newsitem.title: USA: New York spring collections feature more Europeans.
newsitem.headline: New York spring collections feature more Europeans.

text.p: A record number of European designers are previewing their spring collections this week in New York, where the shows have become a stage for the newest and youngest designers.
"Paris is couture, Milan is ready-to-wear and New York is young, cool and modern," said Pam Stein, a spokeswoman for Gianni Versace, whose Versus show kicked off the gala over the weekend.

Draped in clingy, satin-like fabrics in clashing patterns, Versace's pale models marched down the runway like toy soldiers to the beat of booming techno music. The season's hottest look -- 1970s'-inspired, one-shoulder tops -- was in full force.

Like many European designers, Versace, who recently opened a boutique in a former mansion on Fifth Avenue, has chosen New York to preview his secondary, cheaper line of clothing. He is joined this season by compatriots Enrico Coveri and Gianfranco Ferre as well as first-time participants Dolce & Gabbana and Moschino, who will present their D&G and Cheap & Chic lines.
The New York shows are distinct in tone from Paris and Milan, the other two showcases used by the fashion industry.

Shunning the elitism associated with many runway shows, Viacom-owned VH1 television brought fashion to the masses when they aired the second annual VH1 Fashion Awards last Friday, filmed in Madison Square Garden.

Singer Toni Braxton, Gucci designer Tom Ford and actress Gwyneth Paltrow were among the winners honored for their fashion sense on the two-hour program, which will be aired repeatedly throughout fashion week. The gala weeks end on Friday with Donna Karan's main show.
The 7th on Sixth week also spawned spin-off shows and events with a decidedly downtown Manhattan feel.

The "Girls Rule" event, now in its fifth season, showcases funky creations of young local designers. Sunday's show featured punkish models -- including members of the hit Broadway musical "Rent" -- sporting baggy skateboard pants, vinyl dresses and "I dig your boyfriend" underwear.
The arrival of new and European designers comes at a time when top U.S. designers are loosening their ties to 7th on Sixth.

The 7th on Sixth fashion association, formed in 1993 to centralize New York's fashion previews in Bryant Park on midtown Manhattan's Sixth Avenue, has been criticized for cramming too many shows into small spaces, limiting the ability of designers to use lavish sets.
Beginning with last season, Donna Karan and Ralph Lauren opted to strut their stuff on their own, away from the main runways in Bryant Park. Calvin Klein recently announced that he would follow suit.
The three designers remain, however, "associate members" of 7th on Sixth.

A total of 54 fashion houses are slated to participate in the week-long extravaganza. Eight designers, including evening wear maven Bob Mackie and Japanese designer Matsuda, are making their 7th on Sixth debut.

As always, one of the main attractions is star-gazing. Actor Hugh Grant and companion Elizabeth Hurley, actress Mira Sorvino and easy listening crooner Michael Bolton all took in shows over the weekend.
